title: specrails agent profile (v1)
description: Declarative configuration for the specrails implement pipeline. Describes which agents participate, which models they run with, and how tasks are routed to specialists. Consumed by `implement.md` and produced by tools like specrails-desktop. This is specrails-desktop's derivative of specrails-core's canonical v1 profile schema: it adds the optional top-level `provider` field and relaxes `modelAlias` to any non-empty string (provider-catalog validation happens in profile-manager.validateStructural). Per core's schema-identity contract, a diverging vendored copy must carry its own $id — only byte-identical copies may share the canonical core $id.

schemaVersion.description: Profile schema version. v1 is the only supported value at this time.

description.description: Optional short summary of when to use this profile.

provider.description: Optional registered provider id (for example `claude`, `codex`, `gemini`, or `kimi`). When set, the profile's model values are validated according to that provider adapter: normally against its catalog, while adapters that support configured aliases (such as Kimi) accept any schema-valid non-empty alias. When omitted, validation falls back to the project's resolved provider.

model.description: Model used to run the top-level implement orchestrator. The JSON schema accepts any non-empty string; provider-specific validation runs at the structural-check layer (see profile-manager.validateStructural).

agents.description: Ordered chain of agents that participate in the pipeline when this profile is active. Every profile (default + custom) must include the baseline trio (sr-architect, sr-developer, sr-reviewer) — the pipeline depends on all three. Custom profiles add optional agents on top of the baseline. sr-merge-resolver is an optional utility agent and is no longer required.

routing.description: Ordered routing rules. The first rule whose `tags` intersects the task's tag set wins. If a `default: true` entry is present it MUST be the last element. Custom profiles may omit routing entirely — tasks then fall through to the first developer-shaped agent in the chain.

modelAlias.description: Accepted model alias. JSON schema accepts any non-empty string without truncating provider-configured aliases; provider-specific catalog enforcement runs at runtime (see profile-manager.validateStructural).

id.description: Agent identifier. MUST correspond to the selected provider's provider-native role artifact. File-based providers use their own agents catalog (for example `.claude/agents/<id>.md`); Kimi uses the directly discoverable `.kimi-code/skills/<id>/SKILL.md` layout.

model.description: Model override for this agent when this profile is active. When omitted, the agent's frontmatter `model:` is used as a fallback.

required.description: If true, the agent cannot be routed past. Baseline agents (sr-architect, sr-developer, sr-reviewer) SHOULD be marked required. sr-merge-resolver is optional and defaults to required: false.

tags.description: Task tags that trigger this rule. Rule wins if any tag intersects.

agent.description: Agent to route the task to when this rule wins.

default.description: Marks this rule as the terminal catch-all. Exactly one entry with `default: true` is allowed, and it MUST be the last element of `routing`.

agent.description: Agent to route the task to when no earlier rule matched.
